observation.visible_scene: A night waterfront/harbor scene: dark sky above a silhouetted shoreline with low buildings, moored boats, and a row of warm lights along the quay whose reflections shimmer on the calm water. Three firework displays hang in the sky: a left spherical burst of purple dots with short white sparks, a faint central set of vertical spark trails, and a right dome of purple dots with a fan of white falling streaks beneath it.
visible_changes: The left burst's white sparks lengthen and drift downward and slightly left over the clip; its purple dotted shell stays roughly in place but the trailing streaks below it extend and separate.
The right dome's purple-dot crown remains largely stationary while the white streaks fanning out beneath it grow longer, brighter and more spread downward, indicating falling sparks.
The faint central trails also elongate downward.
The water reflections beneath the right and central bursts become noticeably brighter and more defined as the white sparks descend, while the shoreline lights and building silhouettes stay fixed.
Overall brightness of the bursts fades slightly toward the end as the purple dots thin out.
outside_clip_unknowns: The initial launch/explosion of these bursts is not shown; the clip begins mid-descent and the fireworks continue to fall/fade after the last frame.
Whether new bursts appear or these fully extinguish is outside the excerpt.
uncertain_details: Camera appears stationary (background quay lights and buildings do not shift between frames), so the observed motion is the fireworks' own descent rather than camera movement.
The exact color of the sparks (purple vs white) shifts partly with exposure/fading, so subtle hue changes are not firmly distinguishable from brightness decay.
